claim: For tag copy on restore, the console restore flow copies source tags by default (you can uncheck the box to opt out), and in the StartRestoreJob API CopySourceTagsToRestoredResource is false by default, which excludes the original source tags. Restores of DynamoDB, S3, SAP HANA on EC2 instances, virtual machines and Timestream resources currently do not have this feature, and tags are not copied for item-level restores. Some resources have their own rule: for Amazon RDS, tags present at backup time are copied regardless of that parameter (the parameter is used only if the snapshot holds no tags), and Amazon Redshift clusters by default always include tags during a restore job.

qualifiers.scope: tag copy on restore, console versus API
qualifiers.condition: resource types that support tag copy on restore; not item-level restores; RDS and Redshift have their own rules

evidence.quote: When you restore a backup in the console flow, your source tags will be copied by default. In the console, uncheck the box if you wish to opt out of copying tags to a restored resource
In the API operation StartRestoreJob, the parameter CopySourceTagsToRestoredResource is set to false by default, which will exclude the original source tags from the resource you are restoring.
Restores of Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon S3, SAP HANA on Amazon EC2 instances, virtual machines, and Amazon Timestream resources currently do not have this feature available.
Tags will not be copied for item-level restores.

Tags which were present on the resource at the time of the backup will be copied during the restore regardless if the Boolean parameter for `CopySourceTagsToRestoredResource` is set to `True` or `False`. However, if the snapshot does not contain tags, then the above Boolean setting will be used.
**Amazon Redshift** clusters, by default, always include tags during a restore job.
